sentences.text: Seitaad ruessi is the only known species of this sauropodomorph dinosaur, a member of the order Saurischia.
Although the skull is missing, the animal is estimated to have reached a length of 6.5 to 7 meters.
Seitaad holds the distinction of being the second basal sauropodomorph dinosaur identified in North America.
The genus was described by Sertich and Loewen in 2010 based on a single articulated partial postcranial holotype skeleton designated UMNH VP 18040.
Fossils were collected from the Navajo Sandstone near Comb Ridge in San Juan County, Utah, and the name honors a Navajo mythological sand monster.
The species name 'ruessi' commemorates Everett Ruess, an artist and naturalist who disappeared in southern Utah in 1934.
Phylogenetic studies place Seitaad in the family Massospondylidae, though an alternative placement in Plateosauridae is considered less probable.
Fossil evidence dates Seitaad to the Pliensbachian to Toarcian stages, between 192.9 and 174.7 million years ago.
The precise placement of Seitaad within the clade Plateosauria remains poorly understood.
